title: Add cohort susceptibility index and soft-blocker CI hook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Add Cohort Susceptibility Index (CSI) to score prompt cohorts for regression sensitivity.
- Add CI soft-blocker hook that gates merges when CSI + quality delta exceed thresholds (soft-fail with automated rollback suggestion).
- New unit and integration tests; updated docs and runbook for ops response.
description:
Context and motivation:
Small, targeted prompt-set changes have produced outsized regressions on a few high-risk cohorts in production. Existing CI gates surface aggregate regression signals but frequently miss concentrated susceptibility where a low-volume cohort experiences large quality drops. This PR implements a Cohort Susceptibility Index (CSI) plus a CI soft-blocker hook that integrates with the existing eval runner to flag merges that are likely to cause concentrated regressions.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Adds a new metric (CSI) that quantifies cohort-level sensitivity by combining effect size, variance amplification, and token-entropy-weighted failure concentration.
- Adds a CI hook (soft-blocker) that computes CSI + configured quality deltas and returns a soft-fail decision (block for manual review or auto-suggest rollback) rather than a hard pipeline failure by default.
- Wires CSI into the decision layer so team-specific thresholds and hysteresis (entropy hysteresis to reduce flapping) are respected.
- Adds telemetry events and an ops runbook to triage flagged cohorts.

- eval/ci/hooks/soft_blocker.py (new) -- CI hook that calls eval runner, computes CSI, compares against per-team thresholds, emits telemetry, and returns soft-block decision payload

- benchmarks/chi-bench.toml (new) -- bench cases and target SLOs for CSI compute time

Design notes and algorithm summary:
CSI is intentionally conservative: it amplifies effect-size signals for cohorts with high per-example variance and high token-entropy (common failure modes are more critical when model is confident on wrong outputs). The score is a bounded scalar in [0,1] where higher means more susceptible. We use a clamped winsorization on extreme outliers and a sample-size-aware smoothing term so small cohorts do not spike the CSI unless the effect size is large and consistent. Hysteresis: CI stores the last N CSI values per cohort (configurable) and reduces flip-flopping by requiring sustained elevation above threshold for auto-block escalation.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emits chi_evaluation.start / chi_evaluation.end for each CI run with CSI, cohort id, sample size, and contributing metric breakdowns.
- Adds a CSI breakdown panel to existing eval dashboards (instructions in docs).

Review conversation (abridged):

- Maya Chen (author): "Addressed both: added entropy cap in chi.py (entropy_cap config) and added team_opt_out flag in CI hook; updated examples/ci-config.yaml and tests to cover opt-out path."
- Lina Morales (reviewer): "Integration test flaky on CI runner initially, likely due to timeout. Can we reduce synthetic payload size?"

- Samir Gupta (reviewer): "Please ensure runbook includes first responder checklist and Linear template."
- Maya Chen: "Docs updated with Linear template and three-step triage."

CI and validation:
- Initial CI: unit tests passed, integration job failed once due to timeouts on the macstadium runner.
- Rerun: all checks green.
- Performance baseline: CSI compute ~18ms per 1k examples on our CI runner (benchmarks/chi-bench.toml).

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default is soft-fail; teams must opt-in to hard blocking in examples/ci-config.yaml. This prevents accidental pipeline hard failures.
- Rollout: enable telemetry for 1 week for a pilot team, collect flagged cohorts, iterate on thresholds.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash on 2025-02-20 after reviewers approved. Merge commit: "squash: add cohort susceptibility index + CI soft-blocker (ENG-2431)"
